title: 2026 National Defense Strategy
summary: The 2026 National Defense Strategy is organized around four lines of effort: defend the homeland, deter China in the Indo-Pacific, increase allied burden-sharing, and supercharge the defense industrial base. Its research relevance lies in the emphasis on production capacity, sustainment, resilient logistics, and the ability to translate technology into military capability.
key_findings: The defense industrial base is one of four top-level lines of effort.
Deterrence depends on posture, production, sustainment, and allied capacity as well as advanced systems.
The strategy ties modernization to the ability to build, replenish, and support capability at scale.
why_it_matters: It makes industrial capacity and logistics explicit strategic outcomes for the research and technology portfolio.
ftfn_relevance: Supports tracking the transition path from DARPA research to production and sustainment.
Adds a national-security demand signal for manufacturing, materials, energy, and supply-chain evidence.
evidence_limits: The strategy does not identify the performance of specific programs or suppliers.
